cycles.red: the Rust PostgreSQL kernel exposed no domain persistence API and target mutations had no exact Authority route provenance
cycles.green: private tenant transactions now expose bounded Inbox, Effect and Outbox APIs backed by database writer fencing and exact route/object generation

cycles.red: one effect identity reused one nonterminal claim across generations
cycles.green: PostgreSQL derives a distinct canonical claim from effect_id plus its big-endian generation and physical replay proves two generations complete independently

cycles.red: an ambiguous or empty Outbox claim had no immutable command receipt and could be retried with a changed capability
cycles.green: one exact claim operation and immutable per-row receipts distinguish Applied, NotApplied and Conflict, including an empty batch

cycles.red: retry delay and concurrent duplicate transition execution were not part of exact replay truth
cycles.green: retry delay, route provenance, revision, outcome and capability digest bind the command; advisory serialization converges concurrent duplicates to one Applied and one Replay

cycles.red: the target role could call raw generation claim/release functions and legacy raw DML could reach target-provenance rows
cycles.green: target claim/release and raw DML are physically denied; legacy NULL-provenance writes remain compatible while provenance guards reject target mutation

cycles.red: SECURITY DEFINER wrappers trusted a caller-provided claim_id that could strand durable work
cycles.green: claim_id parameters were removed and PostgreSQL derives effect and outbox claim identities from canonical durable identifiers

cycles.red: large-table indexes were declared inside transactional migrations
cycles.green: the migration runner prepares exact indexes concurrently and migration 119 validates validity, uniqueness, columns and predicates
